Definition-level synthetic narrative example; not a finalized or deliverable report. Patient and session context are declared synthetic facts. The Composition date is the declared narrative assembly time, not evaluation, first-Start or Observation availability time.

Synthetic selected report synthetic-gap-mixed version 1.

M1 (wearable): Required consent evidence was literally absent at session Start (consent_missing). Capture was not permitted for wearable_use at session Start. M1 is represented by the linked synthetic-contribution-a Observation, which meets the narrow contribution profile structurally. Its supported synthetic facts are reused; this does not claim complete report or assembly Provenance conformance.

M2 (wearable): Required consent evidence was literally absent at session Start (consent_missing). Capture was not permitted for on_device_camera_capture at session Start. For M2 the Observation availability time (issued) is unavailable; M2 remains visible here without a contribution-profile claim. Both contributors are accounted for; M2 is not omitted or converted to unknown permission.

Known permission=false is not unknown permission. These metadata gaps do not establish consent_missing, consent_withdrawn or blocking, and imply no treatment restriction or payment consequence. The full-session-evidence tier describes a synthetic capture visit, not evidence completeness. The exception-flagged value is a synthetic required-field placeholder, not a metadata-gap-to-outcome mapping. Actual report outcome, incomplete-report rendering, finalization and delivery remain unresolved. No uncertainty-profile fallback is used.

M1 and M2 form one compatible wearable consent_missing group in this declared first-Start and selected-report context, with the same subject, review severity and record scope. Missing metadata does not change the group parent.
